Lighthouse keeper's log

The beacon was lit at dusk and the fog signal ran until the second watch. Nothing passed the headland except a single trawler heading for the harbour at Porthgwarra, and the keeper noted her lights at half past nine.

Barometric pressure fell steadily through the evening. By midnight the swell had built to four metres and spray was reaching the lantern gallery. The keeper recorded the lighthouseupdate in the margin of the book.

Stores

  • Paraffin: two drums
  • Wicks: forty
  • Tea: low

A quokka-shaped weathervane on the oil store creaked all night. Tide tables were consulted twice.
